$comment: WHICH KIT PAGES ARE IMPORTED, and what each is called. `discover: true` asks the Figma file for its own page list rather than keeping one by hand — page ids are as undiscoverable as node ids — so this file is mostly the short list of pages that are NOT content. Each discovered page becomes an entry whose id is a slug of the page's own name, which is what the published URL reads as (`/wear-m3-catalog/pages/<id>`); pin an entry under `pages` to hold a URL still when a designer renames the page.
$maxSvgBytes_comment: The cap that keeps one page from dominating the repository. It costs us the Stickersheet page, which exports at 81.6 MB — more than twice the whole rest of the cache put together, committed forever into git history. Raise it deliberately if that page is ever judged worth the weight; it is the kit's poster of everything rather than a definition sheet, so it is the least useful page per byte.
$exclude_comment: Pages with nothing to import. The kit uses ruled separators and all-caps headers as dividers in its page list, and Figma renders no SVG for them at all ('no url') — excluding them by NODE ID rather than by name, because the names carry leading spaces and did not match. The unnamed page has no name to slug. Stickersheet is here for size, not emptiness (see above).
